title: Monoculture-vs-Polyculture: Does Provider-Lineage Mixing Reduce Shared Jailbreak Susceptibility?

original_idea.body:
# Monoculture-vs-Polyculture

Take public jailbreak prompts; define monoculture (same-lineage) and polyculture (mixed-vendor) panels and measure the fraction of attacks that break ALL members, showing polyculture's lower joint-breach rate. Open models + public attacks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — empirically tests lineage diversity as a systemic-risk mitigation informing procurement/regulation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: run public jailbreaks against mono/poly panels and compute joint-breach rate; standard tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single comparison (joint-breach rate mono vs poly) with clear criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open models + public attacks, no internal access, policy-relevant.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on several open models, light.

novelty.reasoning: Lineage-diversity-reduces-shared-jailbreaks asserted but a clean controlled measurement may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Effect asserted in prior framing; clean mono-vs-poly measurement plausibly open.
